activity_context.topic_title: The Shortest Distance Between a Plane and a Point

feedback.problem: Find the shortest distance between the point $P(-1,11,10)$ and the plane $Π$ with equation $-2x-4y+4z=16.$
feedback.worked_solution:
Let's start by picking a point on the plane. To do that, we simply substitute some concrete values for $x$ and $y$ into the equation and solve for $z.$ Let's choose $x=2$ and $y=3$ (though it doesn't really matter what values we choose). Solving for $z,$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}-2x-4y+4z & =16 \\ -2(2)-4(3)+4z & =16 \\ 4z & =32 \\ z & =8.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we get the point $Q(2,3,8)$ which lies on the plane.

Computing $\overset{\to }{PQ},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{PQ} & =⟨2,3,8⟩-⟨-1,11,10⟩ \\  & =⟨3,-8,-2⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

We also need a normal vector to the plane. For any Cartesian equation of a plane $ax+by+cz=d,$ the normal vector is $n=⟨a,b,c⟩.$ So, for the plane $Π,$ we have $n=⟨-2,-4,4⟩.$ 

Finally, the shortest distance from the point $P$ to the plane $Π$ is the absolute value of the scalar projection of $\overset{\to }{PQ}$ onto the normal vector of the plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =|{\text{comp}}_{n}\,\overset{\to }{PQ}| \\  & =\frac{|\overset{\to }{PQ}\cdot n|}{|n|} \\  & =\frac{|3\cdot (-2)+(-8)\cdot (-4)+(-2)\cdot 4|}{\sqrt{(-2)^{2}+(-4)^{2}+{4}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{|-6+32-8|}{\sqrt{4+16+16}} \\  & =\frac{|\,18\,|}{\sqrt{36}} \\  & =3\end{aligned}
$$
